Q: What is a screen lock on a mobile device?
Option1: A requirement to authenticate before the device can be used after it locks or sleeps
Option2: A feature that lowers screen brightness

Q: What does facial recognition provide on a phone or tablet?
Option1: Biometric unlock by matching the enrolled face
Option2: Automatic contact backups

Q: What are personal identification number codes used for on mobile devices?
Option1: Short numeric codes used to unlock the device
Option2: A code to join a wireless network
Option3: A code to pair a printer
Option4: A code to enable developer mode

Q: What does fingerprint unlock provide?
Option1: Biometric unlock using a fingerprint sensor
Option2: A one time password by text message
Option3: An email alert when storage is full

Q: What is a pattern lock?
Option1: A gesture on a grid that must match the saved pattern to unlock
Option2: A time based code from the cloud

Q: What is a swipe lock?
Option1: A minimal unlock that provides no strong authentication
Option2: A biometric unlock method

Q: What is a remote wipe?
Option1: A command from management or a cloud service that erases device data
Option2: A factory reset using buttons on the device only
Option3: A power cycle of the device

Q: What are locator applications used for?
Option1: Find the device location, ring it, lock it, or display a message
Option2: Improve battery capacity

Q: Why are operating system updates critical on mobile devices?
Option1: They provide security patches that fix known vulnerabilities
Option2: They only change wallpapers

Q: What does device encryption protect on a phone or tablet?
Option1: Stored data from access without authentication
Option2: Only messages in transit
Option4: Only data on a memory card

Q: What are remote backup applications for?
Option1: Copy device data to cloud storage for recovery after loss, theft, or wipe
Option2: Create a local copy on the same device

Q: What are failed login attempt restrictions?
Option1: Policies that add delay, lockout, or wipe after repeated incorrect unlock attempts
Option2: Policies that change wallpaper after a week

Q: What is mobile antivirus intended to do?
Option1: Detect and block malicious applications and behavior on the device
Option2: Increase camera resolution

Q: What is a mobile firewall?
Option1: A rule based filter that controls network connections on the device
Option2: A tool to change fonts

Q: What is a bring your own device policy?
Option1: Rules that govern how personal devices may access company resources
Option2: A policy that issues only company devices
Option4: A policy that disables all wireless networks

Q: What is a corporate owned device policy?
Option1: Rules for devices owned by the organization with mandatory configuration and monitoring
Option2: Guidelines for selecting wallpapers
Option3: Rules for personal social media use

Q: What are profile security requirements on mobile devices?
Option1: Management profiles that enforce passcodes, encryption, updates, and app allow or block lists
Option2: Optional wallpapers and themes

Q: What are Internet of Things devices?
Option1: Embedded networked devices such as cameras, sensors, or thermostats
Option2: Desktop computers running a server

Q: What is an important first step when hardening an Internet of Things device?
Option1: Change default credentials and update firmware
Option2: Disable encryption everywhere
Option3: Expose the device directly to the internet
Option4: Share the same password across all devices

Q: Which network control best limits the impact of a compromised Internet of Things camera?
Option1: Place it on an isolated network segment with limited access
Option2: Enable guest mode on the main wireless network
Option4: Share the device password with the team

Q: A phone with client data is lost. Which two actions protect data and accounts?
Option1: Use device encryption and issue a remote wipe and also revoke application tokens
Option2: Disable the screen rotation setting

Q: A user wants to read company email on a personal tablet. What minimum controls are required?
Option1: Enroll in management, enable encryption, enforce a strong screen lock with attempt limits, require updates, allow remote wipe on separation
Option2: Allow access with no controls for convenience
Option3: Share the company password with the user

Q: Why is a pattern lock often weaker than a personal identification number of the same length?
Option1: Smudge trails and observation make patterns easier to guess
Option2: Patterns are always shorter than numbers

Q: A smart camera is reachable from the internet with default credentials. What is the immediate risk and fix?
Option1: High risk of compromise and change credentials, update firmware, and place it behind a firewall or on an isolated network
Option2: Low risk and leave defaults for convenience
Option3: No risk and defaults are secure

Q: How do locator applications and remote backup work together after a theft?
Option1: Locator helps attempt recovery and remote backup preserves data before issuing a remote wipe
Option2: Locator changes the passcode and backup disables email
Option3: Locator turns off the camera and backup removes apps
Option4: Locator upgrades the operating system and backup reduces storage

Q: A corporate owned phone must block unapproved apps. Which control enforces this?
Option1: A managed configuration profile with an application allow list through mobile device management
Option2: Ask users not to install anything

Q: Why combine failed login attempt restrictions with strong backup practices?
Option1: Aggressive wipe settings can cause data loss if thresholds are reached and backups prevent permanent loss
Option2: It makes the phone charge faster

Q: An employee travels to a high risk region. Which settings reduce exposure if the device is seized?
Option1: Full device encryption, short auto lock timeout, minimal local data, and a plan for immediate remote wipe
Option2: Disable encryption and use a long timeout
Option3: Share the passcode with a manager

Q: How does securing smartphones differ from securing Internet of Things sensors?
Option1: Phones support rich management and user interaction and many Internet of Things devices need network segmentation and simple controls
Option2: They are identical in every way

Q: A smartwatch paired to a company phone displays notifications. What policy should address this?
Option1: Bring your own device or corporate accessory policy that controls pairing and data shown on lock screens
Option2: A policy about keyboard vendors
Option3: A rule that bans all timepieces
Option4: A rule that sets ringtone volume

Q: Why are operating system updates often more important than third party antivirus on phones?
Option1: Updates remediate root vulnerabilities platform wide, while antivirus may not prevent exploitation of unpatched flaws
Option2: Antivirus always reduces battery life
Option4: Antivirus replaces the need for a passcode
